items.title: David Finck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 29, 2015
items.q: And it was an Eddie Palmieri record. And he said, “listen to the bass player.” ... And I tried to do it. I played along with the record.

ctx.x: So that became — I became a student with those guys. I don’t even know if I could do that now. I was pretty good at it then and it’s a different mindset. And now when I listen to a really great Latin jazz bass player like Andy Gonzalez and I hear him play, and I go there’s an accent that he’s got that I don’t have. And a dear friend of mine made me a copy of a beautiful record. Talk about stealing stuff and making illegal copies — but he wanted me to hear this record and he was on it. And it was an Eddie Palmieri…
Yes, and I think you almost have to have grown up with that kind of music. So it’s not foreign. You’re not starting in a foreign place, it’s just a groove you understand.
